title: Prepay, contest or appeal a traffic ticket
question: I got a traffic ticket in Albemarle County. Can I prepay it, how do I contest it, and what if I cannot pay?
office: Albemarle General District Court, Clerk's Office (16th Judicial District)
summary: Most tickets written in Albemarle County go to the Albemarle General District Court, 350 Park Street, Charlottesville. If the offence is on the Supreme Court's Uniform Fine Schedule, you can prepay online (4% card fee; by 3:30 pm the business day before trial), by mail (it must arrive before the court date) or at the Clerk's Office. Prepaying is a guilty plea reported to DMV. Reckless driving (including 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph), DUI, driving suspended or unlicensed, leaving the scene and indictable offences cannot be prepaid. To contest, appear on the summons date; a judge decides an infraction without a jury, and deputy clerks can grant a first continuance. If you cannot pay, the court must offer a payment plan ($10 fee). You can appeal a conviction to the Albemarle Circuit Court within 10 days, with a right to a jury there.

steps.step: Find out which court has the ticket
steps.who: Person charged (the driver named on the summons)
steps.how: The court is named at the top of the summons. A ticket written in Albemarle County is normally returnable to the Albemarle General District Court; a ticket written inside the City of Charlottesville is normally returnable to the separate Charlottesville General District Court, even though both courts sit in Charlottesville. Always use the court named on your summons. Read the NOTICE on the back of the summons and the charge after DESCRIBE CHARGE on the front. If you lost the ticket or do not know which court it went to, search your name in the statewide Online Case Information System (it cannot take payments).
steps.deadline: Before the court date on the summons
steps.quote: If you have lost your traffic ticket (summons) or do not know the jurisdiction in which the summons was issued, you may use the Online Case Information System-Statewide Search to search statewide using your name; however, payments cannot be made using this system.

steps.step: Check whether the offence can be prepaid
steps.how: Only offences listed in the Supreme Court's Uniform Fine Schedule (Rule 3B:2), or a parallel county ordinance, can be prepaid; every other traffic offence needs a court hearing. (State law also lets a non-parallel county traffic ordinance be prepaid if it is on a schedule entered by the circuit court; none was found for Albemarle.) State law bars prepaying indictable offences, reckless driving, driving under the influence, leaving the scene of an accident, driving while suspended or revoked, and driving without a licence. Speeding 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph, is reckless driving, so it cannot be prepaid. If the officer gave you a Virginia Prepayable Offenses Information Sheet, look for your charge in its table. If it is not there, or you got no sheet, call the court for instructions.
steps.quote: For traffic offenses not listed below, a court hearing is required.

steps.step: Decide whether to prepay or to go to court
steps.how: Prepaying is a written guilty plea: you give up the trial, your signed plea has the force of a court judgment, and the conviction is sent to DMV, which may assess demerit points. To contest the charge, do not prepay; appear in court on the summons date (step s10).
steps.quote: Pre-court payments are deemed a waiver of a court hearing and entry of a guilty plea.

steps.step: Work out the amount to prepay
steps.how: The amount is the fine on the Uniform Fine Schedule plus court costs. The schedule sets the same fine everywhere in Virginia (for example, speeding is $6 per mph over the limit, $7 per mph in a school crossing or highway work zone, and $200 plus $8 per mph in a residence district) and lists the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction as its processing fee. Other costs set by statute can be added; for example, a county may add up to $20 for courthouse security if it has adopted an ordinance. No Albemarle General District Court fee sheet was found, so check the total in the online system or call the court.
steps.fee: The fine on the Uniform Fine Schedule plus costs, including the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction (see fees)
steps.quote: This schedule is applied uniformly throughout the Commonwealth, and a clerk or magistrate may not impose a fine different from the amounts shown here.

steps.who: Person charged, paying the Albemarle General District Court
steps.how: Open the General District Court Online Case Information System and choose Albemarle General District Court (the court named on the summons). Search by name, case number or hearing date. If the case shows Mark For Payment, mark it (up to five cases on one receipt), choose Process Payment, pay by credit or debit card, and print the confirmation screen as your receipt. Payments made after 3:30 pm are processed the next business day.
steps.deadline: Before 3:30 pm on the business day before the trial date
steps.fee: Fine and costs, plus a 4% card convenience fee per transaction
steps.quote: Payment must be made prior to 3:30 pm on the business day before the trial date to ensure the payment will be processed before the court date.

steps.how: Follow the PRETRIAL WAIVER AND PREPAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS on the summons and mail the payment to the court named on it: Albemarle General District Court, 350 Park Street, Charlottesville, VA 22902-5113 (the address on the court's page; use the address on your summons if it differs). District courts accept personal checks, money orders, certified checks and credit cards; make a check payable to the court (the state page's example is a county general district court's name). For a card, confirm with the court which cards it accepts, and fill in the Credit Card Authorization on the back of the prepayable offenses sheet if you have one. The payment counts only when the court receives it, and a further fee is added if it arrives after the court date. Do not mail it to the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court.
steps.deadline: It must reach the court before the court date (vacourts.gov advises mailing it at least 7 days before)
steps.quote: Prepayment of the fine(s) and fee(s) is effective only upon receipt by the applicable general district court, not on the date that you mail it.

steps.who: Person charged, at the Albemarle General District Court Clerk's Office (or before a magistrate)
steps.how: Go to the Clerk's Office at 350 Park Street, Charlottesville, during office hours (8:00 am to 4:00 pm). District courts must accept personal checks and credit or debit cards (the clerk may refuse them on limited grounds, such as an earlier dishonoured payment), and the clerk may add a card convenience fee of up to 4% or a flat fee of up to $2. State law also lets you make the written appearance in person before a magistrate before the trial date.
steps.fee: Fine and costs; the clerk may add a card convenience fee of up to 4% (or a flat fee of up to $2)
steps.quote: personal checks and credit or debit cards shall be accepted in lieu of money to collect and secure all fees, fines, restitution, forfeiture, penalties and costs collected for offenses tried in a district court, including motor vehicle violations

steps.step: If you need a new court date, ask for a continuance
steps.who: Person charged, to the Clerk's Office; a judge (or the Commonwealth's Attorney for misdemeanours) decides later or other requests
steps.how: For a traffic infraction, the court's deputy clerks can grant a first continuance; ask for any later one from the judge or the clerk. Continuances of misdemeanour traffic charges (such as reckless driving) are requested from the judge or the Commonwealth's Attorney. Once a continuance is granted in advance, Form DC-344 lets you promise in writing to appear on the new date, so the court shall not require you to appear on the original date. You sign it before a judge, clerk, deputy clerk or notary, and its instructions send the first copy to the attorney for the Commonwealth. The court may still require you to appear on the original date if you are in violation of your pretrial release terms or have failed to appear before.
steps.quote: Traffic first continuance granted by Deputy Clerks; subsequent continuance granted requested from Judge or Clerk;

steps.step: If you cannot attend in person, ask for a remote hearing or an interpreter
steps.who: Person charged (or their lawyer); the judge decides
steps.how: Fill in the court's Motion for Remote Virtual Hearing and send it to the court's email, albemarlegd@vacourts.gov. Whether to hold a hearing by telephone or video is solely within the court's discretion, and you must make sure everyone appearing remotely can connect. Send a copy to the other side and complete the certificate of service, or explain on the form why there was not time to notify them. Ask for a foreign-language or sign-language interpreter before the court date by fax (434-972-4092), email, mail or in person.
steps.deadline: Before the court date (interpreter requests must be made before court)
steps.quote: If you would like to request a remote virtual hearing, please complete the Motion for Remote Virtual Hearing and forward it to

steps.step: To contest the ticket, go to trial on the court date
steps.who: Person charged; an Albemarle General District Court judge decides
steps.how: Appear at the Albemarle General District Court at the date and time on the summons. The court's traffic dockets are Monday and Friday at 9:30 and 10:30 am and Tuesday at 1:00 and 2:30 pm. Cell phones are secured at the courthouse. A traffic infraction is decided by the judge without a jury, and you are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. You can plead guilty, not guilty or nolo contendere, and you can hire a lawyer. Ask the clerk's office to subpoena your witnesses (Form DC-325); the form says requests should be filed at least ten days before trial. If the charge could carry jail time (for example, reckless driving) and you cannot afford a lawyer, the judge may appoint one after examining your finances and your sworn financial statement (Form DC-333); that lawyer's cost is added to your costs if you are found guilty. The fine schedule does not limit the fine the judge can set after a hearing.
steps.deadline: The court date on the summons; witness subpoena requests should be filed at least ten days before trial
steps.fee: If found guilty: the fine the judge sets plus costs, including the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction
steps.quote: You have the right to have the clerk's office subpoena witnesses to appear in court on your behalf.

steps.step: Know what happens if you neither prepay nor appear
steps.how: For a traffic infraction, if you neither prepay nor appear you are deemed to have waived a hearing: the case can be heard without you and you are notified of the finding, but the court shall not issue a failure-to-appear warrant under Va. Code § 46.2-938. A $35 failure-to-appear cost is added unless you ask for a hearing and show good cause. In criminal and certain traffic cases (not infractions), a separate warrant for a new charge of failure to appear may also be issued.
steps.fee: $35 failure-to-appear cost, unless good cause is shown at a hearing you request
steps.quote: In criminal and certain traffic cases, if you fail to pre-pay the fine and costs (when allowed) and also fail to appear in court, a separate warrant may be issued against you on a new charge of failure to appear.

steps.step: After a conviction, pay or ask for a payment plan
steps.who: Person convicted, at the Albemarle General District Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: The court must offer you a payment agreement and tell you about it in writing. Under the court's payment plan policy, a defendant who cannot pay in full within 90 days of the trial date may sign Form DC-210 to enter a deferred plan (pay all at the end), an installment plan (monthly or other periodic payments), or a modified deferred plan. The plan carries a one-time $10 fee. No down payment is needed for an agreement made within 90 days of the court date; the policy asks for one after that, or after a default (see caveats). If your sole financial resource is Social Security or SSI (the policy says sole source of income), tell the court on your request: you are exempt from payments while that is true, and the case will not be sent to collections. You can also petition in writing on Form DC-211.
steps.deadline: Pay in full within 90 days of the trial date or enter a payment agreement, or the account goes to collection; a payment within 10 days of its due date counts as on time
steps.quote: Any Defendant who cannot pay all fines and cost within ninety (90) days of their trial date may sign an Acknowledgement of Suspension or Revocation of Driver’s License (form DC210) to enter into a Deferred Payment Plan, an installment Payment Plan, or a Modified Defined Payment Plan (as described below).

steps.step: Or work off fines and costs with community service
steps.who: Person convicted, by motion; an Albemarle General District Court judge approves
steps.how: File a motion with the court asking to discharge all or part of the fines and costs by community service. The court schedules a hearing on the motion. If the judge approves it, each hour of community service is credited against the fines and costs at the federal hourly minimum wage.
steps.quote: Any person desiring to enter this program shall file an appropriate motion with the Court and be scheduled for a hearing before this court on such motion.

steps.step: Pay later online or by mail, before the account goes to collection
steps.how: Online, in the same General District Court system, from 6:00 am the day after the trial (not on the trial date). By mail, call the court for the amount and your reference case number, write the number on your check, and mail it to the court where the case was heard. Without a payment agreement, an unpaid balance is sent to collection 90 days after the court date, and interest accrues from 181 days after it; no interest accrues while you pay under a court payment agreement.
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the court date, unless you have a payment agreement
steps.fee: Interest after 180 days if unpaid (see fees)
steps.quote: If you have not entered into a “time to pay” or deferred payment agreement and the court has not received your payment within 90 days following your court date, your account will be sent to collection.

steps.step: Appeal a conviction to the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.who: Person convicted, by notice to the Albemarle General District Court clerk; the Albemarle Circuit Court hears the appeal
steps.how: File a notice of appeal with the General District Court clerk within ten days of the conviction, whatever your plea. The Albemarle Circuit Court (Albemarle County Courthouse, Court Square, 350 Park Street) tries the case again from the start, and you have the right to a jury, including for a traffic infraction; check with the Circuit Court clerk about scheduling one. Its criminal terms begin on the first Monday of February, April, June, August, October and December, and criminal cases are set on term day. No new bond is required. You can withdraw the appeal before it is heard by giving written notice to the court and the prosecution, and pay the fine and costs; a withdrawal within ten days of the conviction adds no costs, while a later one leads the Circuit Court to affirm the judgment and tax costs. The court does not forward the conviction abstract to DMV until the appeal period has passed with no appeal perfected.
steps.deadline: Within ten days of the conviction
steps.quote: If you wish to appeal your case to the circuit court, you must file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the general district court within ten days of the judgment or conviction by the general district court.

escalation.quote: At any time during the duration of a payment agreement, the defendant may request a modification of the agreement in writing on a form provided by the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court, and the court may grant such modification based on a good faith showing of need.

escalation.next: Albemarle General District Court, petition for a subsequent payment agreement (down payment capped by statute)
escalation.quote: A defendant who has defaulted on a payment agreement may petition the court for a subsequent payment agreement.

escalation.trigger: Ordered to show cause for not paying
escalation.next: Albemarle General District Court show-cause hearing (the court can allow more time, lower the payments or remit the unpaid amount if the default is excusable)
escalation.quote: the court may enter an order allowing the defendant additional time for payment, reducing the amount due or of each installment, or remitting the unpaid portion in whole or in part.

escalation.trigger: Tried in absence and charged the $35 failure-to-appear cost
escalation.next: Albemarle General District Court, hearing requested by the defendant to show good cause
escalation.quote: a fee of $35 shall be taxed as costs whenever a defendant fails to appear, unless, after a hearing requested by such person, good cause is shown for such failure to appear.

escalation.trigger: Convicted in the General District Court (after trial, in absence, or on a guilty plea)
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court: new trial from the start (de novo, Va. Code § 16.1-136), with a jury available
escalation.deadline: Within ten days from the conviction
escalation.quote: Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.

escalation.trigger: Convicted again in the Circuit Court
escalation.quote: Any aggrieved party may appeal to the Court of Appeals from any final conviction in a circuit court of a traffic infraction or a crime.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, and no county page is relied on here. The court facts come from the court's own pages on vacourts.gov.

County Code. Albemarle County's Code of Ordinances is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, so Chapter 9 (Motor Vehicles and Traffic) has not been checked. The only local-law quote is the title of Board of Supervisors agenda item 21-372 (August 4, 2021), from the county's Legistar records. It describes a proposed recodification in which Article 1 incorporates state law by reference, as Va. Code § 46.2-1313 allows. Legistar holds no action record for that item, so adoption is not confirmed there, and the proposed ordinance itself has not been checked. No circuit court schedule for non-parallel county ordinances (Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(D)) was found.

Costs. No Albemarle General District Court prepayment fee sheet was found on vacourts.gov, and the online case system was not opened, so the court's actual cost total for an infraction is not known. Rule 3B:2's total column adds only the $51 processing fee to the fine. Its fee-column footnote points to Va. Code §§ 9.1-106 and 53.1-120 for other assessments. Whether Albemarle has adopted the courthouse security assessment (§ 53.1-120(D), up to $20) was not confirmed. The Charlottesville court's sheet shows $74.00 in infraction costs, but that is a different court and is not applied here.

Address conflict. The court's vacourts.gov page and its Motion for Remote Virtual Hearing (Rev. 07/24) give 350 Park Street, Charlottesville. The payment plan policy's letterhead (effective July 1, 2024, entered 9/24/2024) gives 501 E. Jefferson Street, Room 138. The court's Directions page describes a building attached to the old county courthouse where Park Street meets East Jefferson Street. Use the address on the summons, or call the court, before mailing a payment.

The court's payment plan policy (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/online/ppp_fines_costs/dc/albemarle.pdf) is a scanned image with no text layer. Its quotes here are transcriptions from the page image, which a text search cannot confirm (one capitalisation was corrected: the policy writes 'an installment Payment Plan'). The policy says Form DC-210 is an 'Acknowledgement of Suspension or Revocation of Driver's License'. DC-210 is not on the vacourts.gov list of district court forms, so the clerk presumably prepares it. Va. Code § 46.2-395 (the former licence suspension for unpaid fines and costs) is not in Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, and whether non-payment can still affect a driver's licence is not covered here.

Possible conflict on down payments. The policy says a down payment is required for an agreement made more than 90 days after the court date. Va. Code § 19.2-354.1(E), as indexed, allows a required down payment only on a subsequent agreement after a default. The policy's percentages (10% up to $500; otherwise 5% or $50, whichever is greater) match the § 19.2-354.1(I) cap for subsequent agreements. Ask the clerk or the judge if a down payment is requested on a first agreement.

The court's continuance policy reads 'subsequent continuance granted requested from Judge or Clerk', which is ambiguous as written; it is quoted word for word. The Commonwealth's Attorney's office handles misdemeanour continuances under that policy, but its own channels are on www.albemarle.org and are not covered here.

The Albemarle Circuit Court's 'Payment Policies for Fines and Costs' link (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/online/ppp_fines_costs/cc/albemarle.pdf) serves a 2015 order and guidelines of the Charlottesville Circuit Court, which name staff. It is not used here. Circuit Court payment rules after an appeal, appeal costs, and the deadline and procedure for an appeal to the Court of Appeals of Virginia are not covered here.

Prepaying is a conviction on a guilty plea. Va. Code § 16.1-132 allows an appeal within ten days 'whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty', but no Albemarle court page says how the ten days are counted after an online or mailed prepayment.

No official Albemarle source says whether the court accepts a driver improvement clinic, community service or other terms in exchange for reducing or dismissing a traffic charge. Va. Code § 46.2-505 lets a court require a clinic after a guilty finding (not for commercial driver's licence holders), and § 46.2-498 covers voluntary clinics. DMV demerit points and insurance effects are not covered here beyond the court pamphlet's statement that DMV assesses points for certain convictions.

Out of scope: school-zone speed camera and school-bus stop-arm citations (civil penalties handled through the county police), county parking tickets, and juvenile traffic cases (Va. Code § 16.1-241, juvenile and domestic relations district court).

The vacourts.gov payment instructions say a card convenience fee of 4% applies online. No Albemarle page states which cards or other methods the Clerk's Office takes at the counter, beyond the statutory duty to accept checks and cards (Va. Code § 19.2-353.3).
The General District Courts Informational Pamphlet (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/courts/gd/gdinfo.pdf) carries a 6/2021 date on its main text and a 10/2024 revision on its ADA notice.
The online payment system (eapps.courts.state.va.us) was not opened; the online steps come from the vacourts.gov instructions page.

The index versions of Va. Code §§ 19.2-354 and 19.2-349 are marked effective until January 1, 2027. Their replacement text was not in the index, so the plan-fee, community service and collection rules may change on that date.

Privacy. The court pages name the clerks and judges; no names are recorded here. The phone (434) 972-4004 appears on the vacourts.gov page after the clerk's name block, and also on the court's own letterhead as its main number, so it is recorded as the office line. The mailbox albemarlegd@vacourts.gov is the court's own published address for remote-hearing motions and interpreter requests.

Rule 3B:2 table rows. The fee row quoted for Va. Code § 46.2-820 ('- failure of driver on left 46.2-820 $30 $51 $81') is the row as it reads across the table columns in the Rules of Court PDF; its text splits the columns otherwise. The residence-district rate ($200 plus $8 per mph) is read from the same table and is not quoted.

Contacts on the vacourts.gov court pages are printed in a block under the clerk's name. The General District Court's (434) 972-4004 and fax (434) 972-4092 are the court's own numbers on its payment plan letterhead; the Circuit Court's main (434) 972-4083 and Criminal (434) 972-4085 lines are labelled office and division lines. They are recorded as office lines; no name is recorded.

Trial in absence. For a traffic infraction, Va. Code § 19.2-258.1 bars a § 46.2-938 failure-to-appear warrant; the pamphlet's warning about a separate failure-to-appear charge is for criminal and certain traffic cases. No Albemarle page says how the court notifies a person of a finding made in absence.

corrections: Quotes: all 87 original quotes were re-checked. The 57 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only), across 19 sections, and each cited subsection letter matches the text. 24 quotes are word for word in the official pages and PDFs re-fetched on 2026-10-11: the vacourts.gov Albemarle GDC page, tickets_dc, the GDC pamphlet, Rule 3B:2 in the Rules of Court PDF and Legistar matter 21-372. The fee row for Va. Code § 46.2-820 is found only in the layout-mode extraction of the Rules PDF, where the table columns line up; a caveat now says so. The six quotes from the scanned payment plan policy were re-read against a 220 dpi rendering.

s12 quote corrected: the payment plan policy reads 'an installment Payment Plan' (lower-case i) and 'Driver’s' (typographic apostrophe); the draft had 'an Installment Payment Plan'. No other wording differed.

Ten state-law quotes added, each checked against I.text_of: § 16.1-69.40:1(A) ('1. Indictable offenses;'), § 46.2-862 (speeds that are reckless driving), § 19.2-353.3 (grounds on which the clerk may refuse checks or cards), § 19.2-266.3 (the exception to waiving appearance), § 19.2-258.1 x4 (judge-only trial of infractions, presumption of innocence, trial in absence with no § 46.2-938 warrant, jury right on appeal) and § 16.1-133 x2 (written notice to withdraw an appeal; affirmance and costs after ten days).

s2: the list of offences that cannot be prepaid left out indictable offences (§ 16.1-69.40:1(A)1) and did not say that speeding 20 mph or more over, or over 85 mph, is reckless driving (§ 46.2-862). Added both, and the § 16.1-69.40:1(D) route for non-parallel county ordinances (no schedule found).

s11: the draft implied a failure-to-appear warrant could follow any missed traffic case. For a traffic infraction, § 19.2-258.1 deems the hearing waived, lets the case be heard in absence with notice of the finding, and bars a § 46.2-938 warrant; the pamphlet's separate failure-to-appear charge applies to criminal and certain traffic cases. Fixed. The step's fee now says the $35 cost applies unless good cause is shown.

s12: 'you sign Form DC-210 with the clerk' changed to 'may sign' (the policy says 'may sign'; it does not say where). 'If your only income is Social Security or SSI' changed to 'sole financial resource', the wording of § 19.2-354.1(J); the policy's 'sole source of income' is noted. The deadline now says to pay in full within 90 days or enter an agreement, rather than presenting 90 days as a limit on asking for a plan (§ 19.2-354.1(B) and (C) require the court to offer one). The same wording fix was made to escalation rung 4.

s6: mailing at least 7 days ahead is advice on vacourts.gov ('should be mailed'), not a rule; the deadline now says the payment must reach the court before the court date and gives the 7 days as advice. Added: confirm with the court which cards it accepts (from tickets_dc).

s7: § 19.2-353.3 says the clerk 'may add' a card fee of up to 4% or a flat fee of up to $2, and may refuse checks or cards on listed grounds. The step said only 'up to 4%'; both now included, with 'may' kept. Returned-check fee amount now says the clerk 'may impose' it.

s8: added from § 19.2-266.3 and Form DC-344 that the continuance must be granted in advance, that the form is sworn before a judge, clerk, deputy clerk or notary, that its instructions send the first copy to the attorney for the Commonwealth, and that the court may still require appearance on the original date after a pretrial-release violation or an earlier failure to appear.
s9: the remote-hearing form also lets the requester say there was not enough time to notify the other side; added.

s10: added the judge-only trial and presumption of innocence (§ 19.2-258.1; the pamphlet also says the GDC holds no jury trials), and that an appointed lawyer's cost is added to costs on a guilty finding (pamphlet). The ten-day witness subpoena timing is the DC-325 form's advice ('should be filed'), not a rule; reworded in how and deadline.

s15: added the jury right on appeal for a traffic infraction (§ 19.2-258.1), written notice of withdrawal to the court and the prosecution, and that a withdrawal more than ten days after conviction leads the Circuit Court to affirm and tax costs (§ 16.1-133). The DMV sentence is now scoped to the conviction abstract (§ 46.2-383(A)).

s1: 'goes to' softened to 'is normally returnable to', with the rule to use the court named on the summons. s4: added the $7 school-crossing and work-zone rate and the residence-district rate ($200 plus $8 per mph) from Rule 3B:2; the residence-district fee item now gives that rate and cites the Rule. The speeding fee item notes the reckless-driving speeds.

Summary updated (indictable offences and reckless-driving speeds not prepayable, judge-only trial of infractions, deputy clerks grant a first continuance, jury on appeal). Three caveats added (Rule 3B:2 table-row extraction, contact lines, trial in absence). Sources added: §§ 19.2-258.1 and 46.2-862.

Checked and left as they were: the court facts on the Albemarle GDC page (hours, address, phone, fax, traffic dockets, cell phones, continuance policy, remote-hearing and interpreter email); the Circuit Court page (address, criminal terms, 'All criminal cases set on Term Day'); the remote-hearing form (interpreter requests by fax, email, mail or in person before court); form titles against the vacourts.gov traffic and criminal forms lists (DC-210 is not listed); and the Legistar matter, whose histories endpoint returns no actions for item 21-372.

Privacy confirmed: no judge, clerk or staff names. The only email is albemarlegd@vacourts.gov, which the court's page publishes three times as the office mailbox. Phones are the GDC main line and fax (both on the court's letterhead) and the Circuit Court's main and Criminal lines; all are office or division lines. Schema: valid JSON in the shape of the other verified place files; step ids s1 to s15 and form ids f1 to f5 are unique, and every step form id exists.
open_issues: County Code Chapter 9 text was not read (Municode not used; albemarle.org answered 403). Adoption of the 2021 recodification (Legistar 21-372) is not confirmed, and no circuit court schedule for non-parallel county traffic ordinances (§ 16.1-69.40:1(D)) was found.

The court's actual cost total for a prepaid infraction is unknown: no Albemarle GDC fee sheet was found, and whether the county adopted the § 53.1-120(D) courthouse security assessment was not confirmed.

Address conflict: the vacourts.gov page and the remote-hearing form give 350 Park Street; the payment plan policy letterhead gives 501 E. Jefferson Street, Room 138. The steps tell the reader to use the summons address or call.
The policy's down payment on agreements made more than 90 days after the court date may conflict with § 19.2-354.1(E); not resolved. Escalation rung 3 covers it.
No page says how the ten-day appeal period (§ 16.1-132) is counted after a mailed or online prepayment.
Whether the 4% card fee applies to a card authorization mailed with a prepayment, or at the counter, is not stated on any Albemarle page.

Circuit Court appeal costs and payment rules, and the deadline and procedure for an appeal to the Court of Appeals, were not researched. The Circuit Court's payment-policy link serves a Charlottesville document.
The index versions of §§ 19.2-354 and 19.2-349 are effective until January 1, 2027; their replacements were not in the index.
